conventions: MAT.3.1-2: the ASV places 'saying' at the end of 3:1, so λέγων (MAT.3.2 s002) is its own unrepresented unit under rule 37 and the target 'saying' (MAT.3.1 t015) is added, each carrying a note naming the other verse. Do not stretch 'saying' onto κηρύσσων in 3:1, and do not stretch λέγων onto Μετανοεῖτε in 3:2. A reference comparison reports λέγων as a disagreement and that report is not a correction.

An English phrasal-verb particle the ASV writes with its verb rides inside that verb's own unit and is never added, and the head stays on the verb word, whether or not the particle answers to a Greek preverb. ἐξεπορεύετο → 'went out' (3.5), ἀνέβη → 'went up' (3.16) and διακαθαριεῖ → 'thoroughly cleanse' (3.12) realize ἐκ-, ἀνα- and δια- under rule 106; ποιήσατε → 'Bring forth' (3.8), ποιοῦν → 'that bringeth not forth' (3.10), ἐγεῖραι → 'to raise up' (3.9), ἐκκόπτεται → 'is hewn down' (3.10) and κατακαύσει → 'he will burn up' (3.12) answer to no preverb and are folded under rules 7 and 27 with the head fixed by rule 17. No expressed Greek preposition competes for any of them, so rule 106's preposition arm is not in question; ἀπό at 3.16 takes its own 'from' beside the participle's 'up', as that rule's own ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος example has it.
report: Checked all 32 candidate lemma groups; every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the source or by the ASV's own wording, so patches is empty. The article ὁ is the only large group and is uniform: unrepresented where the ASV writes a determinerless of/unto phrase (3.1 Ἰουδαίας, 3.2 οὐρανῶν, 3.8 μετανοίας, 3.9 Ἀβραάμ — rules 21, 23), taking 'of the' where a determiner is written (3.7 Φαρισαίων, 3.10 δένδρων); unrepresented before a bare name (3.4, 3.5, 3.9, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15, 3.16) and aligned where the name carries 'the' (3.5 and 3.13 Ἰορδάν-); unrepresented under rule 38 where a demonstrative stands (3.1 ἐκείναις, 3.9 τούτων) and under rule 20 where a possessive or the relative 'whose' does (3.3, 3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.11, 3.12, 3.17); and supplying the pronoun 'he' before a participle at 3.3 and 3.11, with the relativizer left on the participle both times (rules 32, 90).

The likeliest false positive is ποιέω. MAT.3.3 gives 'Make ye ready' to Ἑτοιμάσατε as one support frame headed on ready (rule 66's denominal clause, as ἱκανώσαντι → made meet) and a bare 'Make' to ποιεῖτε with 'straight' standing separately on εὐθείας — the difference is in the Greek, which spells both elements out in the second clause (rule 73's contrast), not in the analysis. MAT.3.8 'Bring forth' and MAT.3.10 'that bringeth not forth' are the same treatment of the same lexeme. Copula and support frames head uniformly on the meaning-bearing word: ἤγγικεν → hand (rules 17, 71, 104), δύναται → able, εὐδόκησα → pleased, πρέπον ἐστίν → becometh.

Verb-adjacent clauses agree across verses: Ἰδών (3.7) and βαπτισθείς (3.16) both keep a supplied 'when', subject and copula inside the participle's unit (rules 74, 86); every finite verb with an unexpressed subject folds its supplied pronoun (3.2, 3.6, 3.7, 3.9, 3.12, 3.15, 3.16, 3.17) while every expressed pronoun takes its own word (3.11, 3.14); anarthrous nouns fold a supplied determiner as a rule 7 helper in all six places (3.3 φωνή and κυρίου, 3.10 πῦρ, 3.16 πνεῦμα and περιστεράν, 3.17 φωνή) and rule 58 gives it to the noun in both adjective-plus-noun phrases (3.4 ζώνην δερματίνην, 3.11 πνεύματι ἁγίῳ). πᾶς at 3.10 is not rule 87's case: the ASV writes 'every … not' in two words, so the pair splits as that rule requires.

I read the dump end to end for the split the lemma table cannot see. The chapter has exactly two added units and they are structurally distinct — MAT.3.1 'saying' under rule 37 and MAT.3.16 'unto him' under rule 97, whose note carries the unit id, the excluded r00-base the projection holds, the surviving r01/r02, and the ASV's own omission note. Every other supplied English word is folded onto a licensing token: the italic 'in' at 3.11 t036 onto πυρί (rule 103's repeated function word), the italic 'it' at 3.15 t008 onto Ἄφες (rule 74's supplied object), 'to our' at 3.9 onto Πατέρα, 'even' at 3.10 onto ἤδη. Nothing is added in one verse and folded in another.

BSB: all four disagreements are documented convention differences and none is a genuine error. MAT.3.2 τῶν and MAT.3.9 τῷ are rule 21's determinerless clause, the ASV writing 'of heaven' and 'unto Abraham' with no determiner for the article to anchor. MAT.3.2 καί is a connective the ASV does not render at that seam (114 unrepresented καί in the corpus). MAT.3.2 λέγων is rule 37, which says in terms that such a report is not a correction. No accepted edge was touched.

One hedged unit stands and is worth a later reader's attention: MAT.3.15 joins πρέπον ἐστίν as one aligned unit for the single English 'becometh', headed on πρέπον, its note conceding the split reading that would leave ἐστίν unrepresented. It is the chapter's only periphrasis of that shape, so I did not generalise from it.
